parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing criminalisation, entry, facility, custody or care exclusion is documented, and national anti-discrimination protections plus courts recognising hate motive and prosecuting dating-app ambushes in 2025 are operative. Likelihood of outing is not state-engineered; severity if outed is mainly societal harassment and a documented dating-app ambush/robbery pattern, with many incidents unreported and hate-crime recording absent, hampering recourse. The capital-region medical-certificate conflict is unresolved but resident-facing and not shown to affect foreign visitor documents. Combined regime is therefore strongly protective with material street-level residual risk.

entry_documents.protection: National self-determination procedure continues per justice department despite 2019 partial annulment; no visitor document rejection documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Resident registration conflict does not extend to traveller passport on available evidence.

investigation_detention_custody.protection: No trans-specific detention, custody placement or verification practice documented.

federal_state_facilities.protection: No bathroom, ward or public-facility restriction for trans visitors documented.

care_services.protection: Conversion practices banned 2023 with penalties; no visitor care denial documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminal offence documented; institutional hostility largely absent.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Discrimination, hate crime and hate speech on gender identity prohibited; hate motive recognised in court.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Absent statutory hate-crime definition/recording code means offences prosecuted under general provisions, weakening identification.

minors_guardians.exposure: No visitor-specific minor restriction documented. Resident 16-17 marker change needs parental consent and psychological opinion.
minors_guardians.interaction: Resident minor route does not govern a visiting minor's home documents on available evidence.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Rising violence/intimidation reported, trans people especially affected; recurring dating-app traps leading to ambush, robbery, humiliation or assault; many unreported.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police record incidents; May 2025 capital court case against three men accused of targeting at least eight victims; 2014 hate-motivated murder conviction.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Traveller using dating apps faces documented ambush risk, but prosecution shows some functioning recourse, undermined by under-reporting and no hate-crime recording.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: 136 equality-body cases in a year: 35% physical assault, 35% serious intimidation; case mix, not population rate. 2019 capital survey: 90% LGBT verbal/psychological harassment.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Formal prohibition and court recognition of hate motive.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Prevalence figures are dated, LGBT-wide and case-based, so weight is limited; remedy effectiveness for visitors is uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.85-A: that anchor has prompt disciplinary remedies and only isolated friction, whereas this dossier documents rising violence, recurring app ambushes, under-reporting and no hate-crime recording code.

Similar to 0.75-D in that street attacks can occur and remedy depends on reporting, but higher because no brief detention, facility exclusion or officer discretion exposure is documented and formal protections are broader.
Higher than 0.65-C: no border/police detention or extortion pattern, no imprisonment threat, and courts have recognised hate motive and prosecuted ambush cases, though recording gaps remain.

parsed.synthesis: National protections form the operative base: no traveller-facing state exposure at entry, facilities, custody or care is documented, and foreign documents are not shown to be doubted despite a local resident-registration conflict. The main interaction is societal: dating-app use can lead to ambush, and harassment/intimidation reports are rising, but police recording and a 2025 prosecution demonstrate partial recourse. Absent hate-crime definition and recording, plus under-reporting, prevent a higher score; absence of state targeting, criminalisation or universal-exposure measures prevents a materially lower one.
